title: 修复之前：读懂条件
author: BOOKLOOP 原创共读练习（AI 辅助编写）
rights: 本站原创教学练习；来源链接为延伸阅读，正文并非该来源原文或引文。
description: 材料再利用主题馆 · 练习区分条件、证据和个人判断；不作为实际维修操作指南。
paragraphs: A repair may extend an object's useful life, provided that the repaired object remains suitable for its intended use.
In this sentence, provided that introduces a condition. The sentence does not promise that every repair is safe or useful. What information would you need before applying it to a real object?
A visible improvement is not, by itself, evidence that a repair has restored the object's original performance.
Compare two claims: the object looks better, and the object performs as required. Explain what evidence would support each claim, and what remains unknown.
Leave the next reader a note that separates what you observed, what you inferred, and what you still need to check.
Reading task: choose one sentence, ask a precise question, and support your reply with a reference to this text or a source you have checked.

title: 再利用：比较的边界
author: BOOKLOOP 原创共读练习（AI 辅助编写）
rights: 本站原创教学练习；来源链接为延伸阅读，正文并非该来源原文或引文。
description: 材料再利用主题馆 · 练习理解替代关系；不预设减排数字或效果。
paragraphs: To evaluate a reuse proposal, first describe the alternative it is being compared with. Reusing an object and avoiding a new purchase are not necessarily the same event.
The word necessarily matters. It leaves room for situations in which the proposed reuse does not replace the activity assumed in the comparison.
A useful explanation names its assumptions. It also identifies the information that could change its conclusion.

Reading task: write your first interpretation, discuss the sentence with another reader, and record which part of your interpretation changed. A disagreement can be informative even when it remains unresolved.
